title: The Quiet Tryouts
premise: Beatrix Oyelaran, a debate champion drowning in her parents' expectations and counting days to graduation, finds her late grandmother's recipe box hiding spell-cards instead of recipes — an invitation to the Quiet Tryouts, a hidden competition where magical heirs are sorted into found families called Circles. As Beatrix trains for both the state debate championship and the Tryouts' final Trial before prom, she discovers her Circle's mentor is harvesting winners' borrowed magic to fuel his own immortality. In the end, Beatrix loses the debate that doesn't matter on purpose, wins the Trial that does by refusing to use stolen power, and chooses a family that chose her back.
about_author: Rosalind Quintana is a former high-school forensics coach who swears every tournament cafeteria hides at least one secret society. She writes from a kitchen table crowded with recipe cards, most of which are actually for food.

chapters.title: The Recipe Box That Hums
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. While avoiding another dinner-table argument about her future, she sorts her grandmother's recipe box and finds cards written in ink that moves — directions for 'gathering quiet,' 'borrowing breath,' 'unseen entry.' Emotional beat: restless curiosity cracking through resignation.

chapters.title: Counting Days
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. A brutal day: losing a practice debate to her smug teammate Dev, then coming home to parents who've already chosen her college major. She recites her countdown — 94 days to graduation. Beat: invisibility as armor, and its cost.

chapters.title: The Card That Works
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Half-joking, she follows the 'unseen entry' card in the school library and walks through a wall into a candlelit annex where other students wait. Beat: terror giving way to the first flush of belonging.

chapters.title: The Quiet Tryouts
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Proctor Adaeze explains the Tryouts: seven trials, no applause, winners join Circles of five who share magic like a meal. Her grandmother was a Trial champion. Beat: grief and hunger entwined — Grandma left this for her.

chapters.title: First Trial: Borrowed Breath
chapters.summary: Alternating Beatrix and Dev POVs. The first trial asks competitors to hold a stranger's memory without losing their own. Beatrix excels; Dev, also secretly competing, notices her slipping away between classes. Beat: two rivals circling the same secret.

chapters.title: Circle of Strays
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. She's drafted into a Circle with four misfits: anxious Theo, sharp-tongued Priya, gentle Marcus, and silent June. Their first shared ritual feels more like home than her own kitchen. Beat: found family's first warm shock.

chapters.title: Debate Season Interlude
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. At the regional qualifier, Beatrix deliberately underperforms to protect her secret, and Dev covers for her — why? His own mother vanished after winning a Trial years ago. Beat: rivalry softening into wary alliance.

chapters.title: Second Trial: The Unwitnessed Argument
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Competitors must win an argument no one can hear or see. Beatrix realizes the trial mirrors her home life — she's been debating into silence for years. Beat: painful self-recognition as power.

chapters.title: Mentor Malachi's Generosity
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Charming mentor Malachi offers the Circle extra training, gifts, shortcuts. Priya notices he never lets them see him tired, and that his hands are cold. Beat: charm with hairline cracks.

chapters.title: Third Trial: What You'd Trade
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Each competitor must offer a true sacrifice; June gives up her voice for a week, and Beatrix carries her words for her. Beat: love as labor — the Circle becomes real through cost.

chapters.title: Homecoming Fracture
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Her mother finds a moving recipe card and burns it, calling Grandma's things 'nonsense.' Beatrix, for the first time, argues back and wins — and hates how it feels. Beat: victory without witness tastes like ash.

chapters.title: Fourth Trial: The Mirror Stand
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Competitors debate themselves. Theo nearly drowns in his own doubt until Beatrix's steadying presence anchors him. Beat: the Circle learning they're each other's ground.

chapters.title: Dev's Discovery
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Digging into his mother's disappearance, Dev finds Malachi's name in old Tryout rosters going back decades — unaged. He brings the evidence to Beatrix. Beat: dread replacing ambition.

chapters.title: Fifth Trial: The Stolen Round
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Malachi encourages the Circle to draw power from eliminated competitors 'who won't miss it.' Beatrix refuses; Priya accepts and grows terrifyingly strong overnight. Beat: the corruption theme made intimate — power offered by someone you trust.

chapters.title: Prom Dress, Empty Chair
chapters.summary: June's POV. Prom planning collides with Trial prep; June, voice returned, confesses she saw Malachi drain an eliminated girl in the annex. The Circle must decide: report him and forfeit, or play his game to the final. Beat: loyalty tested against survival.

chapters.title: Sixth Trial: Silence
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The trial strips all magic; competitors face only their plain selves. Beatrix, stripped of borrowed strength, discovers what's genuinely hers — her listening. Beat: humility as the true prize.

chapters.title: State Championship
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. The debate final Beatrix has trained years for. Mid-round, she learns Malachi has taken June. She concedes the match on purpose and walks out mid-sentence. Beat: choosing the championship that matters over the one that doesn't.

chapters.title: The Seventh Trial
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The final Trial before prom: Malachi reveals himself as judge and predator, demanding the Circle surrender their bond-magic to 'graduate.' Beatrix counters with the one argument he can't answer — a Circle that refuses to be harvested. Beat: climax; the debate champion finally argues for something real.

chapters.title: What Power Owes
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya, corrupted by stolen power, must choose between Malachi's promise of greatness and the friends she betrayed. She turns her borrowed magic against him, collapsing his long life all at once. Beat: redemption purchased at terrible price.

chapters.title: Aftermath in the Annex
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. The Tryouts dissolve; freed magic returns to its givers, including a flicker of Dev's mother's memory that tells him she didn't leave by choice. The Circle buries Grandma's box together. Beat: grief shared is grief halved.

chapters.title: Prom
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. No crowns, no trials — just bad music and the five of them plus Dev, awkward and laughing. Her parents, changed by her standing up, wait up with questions instead of verdicts. Beat: belonging chosen, not assigned.

chapters.title: The Next Quiet
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV, epilogue. Graduation day; she counts days no more. A new humming recipe card arrives addressed to June's little sister — the Tryouts will need new keepers. Beatrix smiles: some families you're born into; others you build and defend. Beat: hopeful, open-ended close.
